# navig-vm

<!-- navig:plugin-card:start -->
<!-- Generated by scripts/gen_plugin_catalog.py — edit the plugin's pyproject.toml, not this block. -->

> Local VMware Workstation VMs from verified cloud images, provisioned on first boot with cloud-init and driven from `navig vm` (create, start, ssh, snapshots).

**Works on its own** — its own CLI, no navig required · v0.1.1 · not on PyPI yet (install from source below)

**On its own** (no navig needed)

```bash
pip install "git+https://github.com/navig-run/plugins#subdirectory=navig-vm"
navig-vm --help   # no navig needed
```

**With navig**

```bash
pip install "git+https://github.com/navig-run/plugins#subdirectory=navig-vm"
navig vm --help
```

<details><summary>Commands</summary>

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `navig vm console` | The VM's serial console: kernel, systemd and cloud-init output, as text. |
| `navig vm create` | Build a VM from a cloud image: disk, first-boot seed, its own SSH key. |
| `navig vm destroy` | Delete a VM and its folder. Only ever a folder navig created under the VM root. |
| `navig vm exec` | Run one command in the VM; its exit status is this command's. |
| `navig vm ip` | The VM's IP address (reported by VMware Tools in the guest). |
| `navig vm list` | Every VM navig built, and whether it is running. |
| `navig vm password` | The guest owner's password (for the login screen and sudo). |
| `navig vm push` | Copy local files into the VM (scp, as its owner); its exit status is this command's. |
| `navig vm revert` | Go back to a snapshot (the VM is powered off afterwards; start it again). |
| `navig vm screenshot` | Save a PNG of the VM's screen (needs VMware Tools running in the guest). |
| `navig vm snapshot` | Save the VM's current state under a name. |
| `navig vm snapshots` | The VM's snapshots. |
| `navig vm ssh` | Open a shell in the VM as its owner (extra arguments run as a command). |
| `navig vm start` | Power a VM on. |
| `navig vm stop` | Shut a VM down (cleanly, through the guest, unless --hard). |
| `navig vm wait` | Wait until first-boot provisioning has finished (and, for navig-os, the reboot). |

</details>

<!-- navig:plugin-card:end -->

Local virtual machines on **VMware Workstation**, built from a verified cloud image in one
command and set up on first boot by cloud-init — then driven from the terminal.

```sh
navig vm create lab                      # Debian 13, 4 CPU, 8 GB, 40 GB, owner = your user name
navig vm create srv --image ubuntu-24.04 --headless   # Ubuntu Server 24.04 LTS instead
navig vm wait lab                        # until first-boot provisioning is done
navig vm ssh lab                         # a shell, with this VM's own SSH key
navig vm snapshot lab clean
navig vm revert lab clean                # back to it any time
```

Runs inside navig as `navig vm`, or on its own as `navig-vm` (`pip install navig-vm`).

## A NAVIG OS lab machine

```sh
navig vm create navig-os-lab --recipe navig-os --repo <signed NAVIG apt repo folder> --keyboard fr
navig vm wait navig-os-lab
navig vm snapshot navig-os-lab fresh-install
```

The `navig-os` recipe shares the repository folder into the VM, installs the NAVIG OS
packages from it with the same installer an existing Debian machine uses, and reboots
into a login screen offering **NAVIG OS** (full screen) and **GNOME** (the desktop, with
NAVIG OS as an app). Build the repository with `apps/os/linux/build-all.sh`.

## How a VM is built

1. Downloads the cloud image once and checks it against the publisher's sums (Debian:
   SHA-512; Ubuntu: SHA-256).
2. Debian ships a raw disk: a VMDK descriptor points at it. Ubuntu ships a VMDK, used
   as-is. Either way `vmware-vdiskmanager` converts it to a growable disk and grows it to
   `--disk` GB (cloud-init grows the partition at boot). No third-party tool is needed.
3. Writes a cloud-init seed ISO (label `CIDATA`): the owner account (password stored only
   as a SHA-512 hash), a fresh SSH key for this VM, and the recipe.
4. Writes the `.vmx` — UEFI, PVSCSI, vmxnet3 on NAT.

Each VM is a folder under `~/Documents/Virtual Machines` (change it with
`navig config set plugins.vm.dir <folder>`) holding the VM, its own `id_ed25519` and
`known_hosts`, and `navig-vm.json`. Your personal SSH keys and known_hosts are never used
or touched. `destroy` deletes only a folder navig created there.
